# mio CLI — machine-readable command index
# Format: mio <resource> [sub-resource] <action> — purpose
# Auth: export MIO_API_KEY=mio_sk_live_<key>  (exit 3 if missing/invalid)
#       resolution order: --api-key flag > MIO_API_KEY env > OS-keychain key (mio login); --anonymous forces unauthenticated — it SENDS the request with no Authorization header and lets the API answer (a 401 under it is the server's verdict, not a local precondition; whoami reports key_source "none (--anonymous)"), an explicit --api-key still wins (MIO-2694)
#       key auth works against https://api.member.dev; override with MIO_API_BASE_URL or --api-base
# Config: TOML at ~/.config/mio/config.toml ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mio/config.toml); keys: current_team|current_hub|api_base
# Output: JSON by default when piped; --output json|table|plain; --jq <expr>; --raw for envelope
# CAPTURING A STRING ID: add -o plain (MIO-2792). --jq renders through the JSON formatter, so a STRING result is JSON-QUOTED and $(...) captures the quotes — HUB_ID=$(mio hubs list --jq '.[0].id') yields "019f…" which then 404s downstream. Use `-o plain --jq` for every string capture; numeric captures (draft_version, counts) are unquoted either way.
# Destructive ops (delete|cancel|refund|member-moderation: ban|unban|warn|soft-ban|community moderation reports resolve): require --yes/-y in non-interactive shells (exit 5 otherwise). restore is an undo, not destructive — no --yes needed.
# Exit codes: 0=ok 1=error 2=bad-args(400/409/422) 3=auth(401/403) 4=not-found 5=needs-confirm 6=rate-limited(429) 7=server(5xx). Deliberately COARSE — for the exact status the API returned (403 vs 401, 409 vs 422) read errors[0].status from the stderr JSON:API envelope, which carries the real HTTP status verbatim; errors[0].meta.exit_code echoes the coarse code. Local failures that never reached the network have no HTTP status and fall back to the exit code's class. VERSION GATE (MIO-2656): the real-status behaviour lands in the release AFTER v0.12.1 — on v0.12.1 and earlier errors[0].status is reconstructed from the exit code, so 403 reports "401", 409 and 422 both report "400", 503 reports "500" and 405/415 report "500"; check `mio version` before branching on it. Exit codes and meta.exit_code are unchanged on every version
# NOTE: this index tracks `main`, not the released binary — you may be reading it against an older installed mio. Run `mio version`; `mio <cmd> --help` and `mio gen-docs` come from YOUR binary and never skew. Behaviours newer than the latest release are marked with a VERSION GATE.
# Full reference: mio gen-docs --dir ./docs  (one Markdown file per command)
# Agent skill: mio skills print (the full hub-authoring recipe + render-contract traps); mio skills install drops it into Claude Code/Codex
#
# PAGE-TREE RENDER CONTRACT (the API validates STRUCTURE, not RENDERABILITY — these all 200 and then FAIL DIFFERENTLY: some drop the node, some discard one setting and render the node anyway; the entries below say which):
#   node envelope: {id, kind, template?, value?, settings{}, children[]} — VALUE IS TOP-LEVEL, NOT settings.value (the #1 silent drop — now CAUGHT CLIENT-SIDE by `pages tree set`, exit 2 before any HTTP; progress-ring is the sole kind reading settings.value)
#   the renderer dispatches on `kind`, never `type`; `template` marks a section (publish-time conversion + surface wrapping); no defaults cascade — inline every value; exactly one level:1 headline per page (extras demote to h2)
#   value-bearing kinds (the 7 whose top-level `value` the renderer reads): headline text image video button icon quote — divider reads no value at all, and progress-ring reads settings.value (a number), which is why the pre-flight allowlist has seven entries (quote's value is an OBJECT {quote,name?,profession?,avatarUrl?,avatarFallback?} and renders nothing unless .quote is a non-empty string; progress-ring reads settings.value instead). The FULL node-kind + settings vocabulary is GENERATED from the catalog's settingsSchema into the agent skill (mio skills print) — do not transcribe it here. NOT node kinds: subheadline paragraph embed html spacer stat input sidebar section (removed from the FE or never existed — authoring one renders blank; use headline level:3, text, and container gap instead). content-grid is a TEMPLATE id, not a kind. A sidebar = a `row` whose `stack` children set settings.width (full|1/2|1/3|2/3|1/4|3/4)
#   settings.weight must be a NUMBER (700), never "bold" — a non-numeric weight is DISCARDED and the kind's fallback applies (headline 400/normal, text no weight class), so the node RENDERS with the wrong weight rather than disappearing (MIO-2799); section `template` must be a non-empty string — `pages tree set` rejects all THREE client-side (exit 2, no HTTP): a non-numeric weight, a blank/non-string section template, and a content value placed under settings.value on a kind that reads the top-level one (MIO-2575)
#   button: value=label; settings.action={"type":"url|page|email|scroll|playlist","value":"<canonical FOR ITS TYPE>"} — `url` takes a FULL URL INCLUDING the scheme (https:/http:/tel:/sms:) and is passed through untouched, so a schemeless value renders a non-navigating button; `email` takes a bare address (the FE adds mailto:), `scroll` a bare anchor id (it adds #), `page` a system page type/UUID//-prefixed path, `playlist` a playlist id; optional action.params is a string map merged onto the href; icon: value=glyph name (NOT settings.name); image/video: value=the URL
#   settings.surface = {padding, background, gradient}. background.type enum: tint (light tint of branding.secondary — the only value scaffolds emit) | color+token(primary|secondary|accent|muted|background; primary also stamps data-bg="primary" → bold band + primary-button auto-inversion) | custom-color+value(#rrggbb) | gradient | image+url(+blur; the secondary scrim is ALWAYS composed over the image and is not authorable) | none. `thumbnail` is NOT valid — the catalog excludes it deliberately (declared as a TODO in hub types, implemented nowhere, used by no recipe), so authoring it takes the off-enum path. TRAP: an INVALID background.type is accepted on publish and renders a TRANSPARENT row with NO error (renderer default case) (MIO-2663)
#   TRAP: the gradient config is a SIBLING of background — surface.gradient, NOT surface.background.gradient; nesting it silently falls back to the default `split`. gradient.type: monochrome|analogous|complementary|triadic|split|warm-shift|custom (custom REQUIRES customStart+customEnd 6-digit hex, else falls back to split)
#   surface wrapping is NARROWER than the template list: a template opts in by DECLARING a `surface` property in the catalog (presence is enough, even {}) — hero carousel grid content-grid row search-bar compact testimonials (8; content-card is the only section template that does NOT). Derived from the catalog, generated into the skill. There is no `scroll` section type — "Scroll" is only compact's label
#   tree WRITE limits (422, not a silent drop): <=500 elements counting every child incl. malformed ones; root must carry a `children` array; children/settings/dataSource when present must be array/object/object. Every node needs an `id` (root's is optional to the validator) and NO format is enforced — the catalog's own starters ship id:"root"; ids must be UNIQUE within the tree, which is how splicing two scaffolded subtrees collides
#   SYSTEM KINDS: the FE registry renders 10 kinds the catalog deliberately omits (login-form register-form onboarding-form account-profile-form account-activity-feed member-directory-list discussion-list notification-feed achievement-list leaderboard). They are SystemKinds requiring system:true and the PAGE-TYPE ROUTE injects them — the catalog's page templates hand you only the surrounding editable slots (page-login's starter is editable-top + editable-bottom, no form node). The backend validator checks shape not kinds so one would be STORED, but scaffold the matching page-* template and fill its slots instead of hand-authoring an undocumented contract
#   `mio pages publish` returns section_count — compare it to the number of sections you authored; that, not the 200, is the "did it apply" signal (MIO-2539)
#
# HUB BRANDING KEY MAP: primary=buttons/links/CTAs; secondary=THE PAGE'S INK, not a decorative accent — in light mode --hub-text: var(--hub-secondary) so it colors every heading AND all body copy, and it is the base of every surface.background:{"type":"tint"} block; in dark mode it becomes the page BACKGROUND (set it light and the whole page goes invisible — the most common branding mistake); text=body copy; background=page background; header_color/header_accent=top-nav bg+accent (emitted raw, no contrast correction); dark_mode=bool but it selects NOTHING (it only flips the DEFAULTS for background/text, which light/dark mode then discards anyway). branding.text and branding.background are HONOURED ONLY when the theme mode is `custom`: the theme layer emits --hub-text/--hub-background from them only for mode=custom, and in light/dark it CLEARS both and derives them from secondary (light: bg white, text=secondary; dark: bg=secondary, text white) — so to control them directly pass --settings-json '{"background":{"type":"custom"}}' too, where text is additionally AA-clamped against background. COLOR VALUES must be 6-DIGIT hex for all six color keys (primary, secondary, background, text, header_color, header_accent): the FE parser tests /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/ and silently substitutes its own default on anything else, so 3-/8-digit hex, named colors, rgb()/hsl() and gradients all render wrong with a 200 on the wire (a RENDER contract, not an API one — the CLI does not validate values, conduit rule). THEME: A HUB CANNOT SELECT LIGHT OR DARK — ONLY `custom`. resolveThemeMode() consults the hub's mode for exactly one value (`if (hubMode === 'custom') return 'custom'`); otherwise light vs dark comes from the VIEWER's mio-hub-theme cookie (default 'system') and their OS prefers-color-scheme. Writing light/dark anywhere on the hub is a NO-OP, and there is NO settings.theme key either (the FE's parsed theme.mode is DERIVED from settings.background.type). `custom` IS honoured unconditionally via --settings-json '{"background":{"type":"custom"}}', and it is the ONLY mode in which branding.background/branding.text are read at all — in light/dark the theme layer clears both and derives them from secondary (light: bg white, text=secondary; dark: bg=secondary, text white), and in custom mode text is AA-clamped against background. branding.dark_mode selects nothing
# NAV ICON GLYPHS (MIO-2675, CLI passes them through unvalidated): header/footer accept any id from the hub FE icon sprite (~205; generated ICON_NAMES in mio-hub src/components/ui/icon.tsx is authoritative) and `icon` is OPTIONAL — an unknown name drops the icon, not the item; `info` and `globe` DO NOT EXIST (use information/information-circle, earth/global). mobile accepts an 8-VALUE WHITELIST and `icon` is MANDATORY (off-list → the whole tab is dropped): Home Bell User Users MessageSquare MessageCircle Search content — FE component names, not sprite ids, casing significant. <3 valid mobile tabs → the FE replaces the list with its defaults; >5 → truncated to 5

mio version — print version information
mio update — self-update mio; --version pins a release; --prefix chooses install dir. macOS/Linux rerun the official release installer; Windows updates natively (download + SHA-256 verify against checksums.txt + binary swap) with no sh/curl dependency, leaving mio.exe.old behind until the next run. WINDOWS GATE (MIO-2873): `mio update` is executed by the updater compiled into the INSTALLED binary, so on v0.12.1 and earlier it still fails regardless of what a later release fixed — usually `exec: "sh": executable file not found in %PATH%`, but `curl or wget is required to update mio` when neither is on %PATH% (the pipeline LookPaths curl/wget before it execs sh); Windows 10 1803+ ships curl.exe so the first is the common case, and BOTH mean the same thing: you are running a pre-0.13.0 updater — those users need ONE manual install from the releases page, after which updates work; the failure is clean and leaves mio.exe intact. AGENT SKILL (MIO-2874/2875): after a successful update the skill is refreshed BY THE NEWLY INSTALLED binary, not by the running one — the skill body is compiled into each release, so the old process holds only the old surface and re-stamping it with the new version string would produce old content under a new label WITH a matching content hash, i.e. a skill that lies with no mismatch signal. The skill path (~/.claude/skills/mio/SKILL.md, or $CODEX_HOME/skills/mio/SKILL.md — ~/.codex/... when CODEX_HOME is unset) is OUTSIDE --prefix. It is named in the output WHEN THE FILE CHANGES; when the skill is already current the update says NOTHING about it, so absence of a skill line means 'already current', not 'failed' — a failure or a skipped hand-edited file always prints. NOTE the DERIVED BINARY PATH (prefix + mio) is made absolute before the handoff, though --prefix itself reaches the installer verbatim: filepath.Join(".","mio") yields the separator-free "mio", which os/exec resolves through $PATH, so `mio update --prefix .` would otherwise hand the refresh to a DIFFERENT mio on PATH and report its version as installed. A hand-edited or non-mio file at that path is never overwritten — the update reports it PER TARGET, naming the path, and gives the command for that target (`mio skills install --force --target claude|codex`). The --target is load-bearing and omitting it can DESTROY DATA: --force alone defaults to claude, so running it for an edited codex skill acts on the claude file instead — answering 'already up to date' (a current claude skill exists), CREATING a claude skill you never had (none exists), or OVERWRITING your hand-edited claude skill (one exists and you had edited it). Measured: a sentinel in a hand-edited claude SKILL.md was gone after the bare form. Always pass the --target the CLI printed. An unreadable skill file is reported too, not silently skipped. If the refresh cannot run at all, that is reported rather than leaving a silently stale skill, because a stale skill advertises verbs the installed binary may not have and the failures read as CLI bugs rather than version skew. There is no freshness check on an idle skill — if yours predates your binary, run `mio skills install`
mio skills install — install the embedded mio agent skill into your coding agent; --target claude|codex (default claude); --user (default) or --project; --force overwrites a hand-edited file; idempotent
mio skills print — print the embedded mio agent skill (SKILL.md) to stdout; --target claude|codex
mio login — interactive login (stores key; auto-resolves team for single-team accounts); use MIO_API_KEY instead in agents
mio register — create a new account (email+password, optional --first-name/--last-name; or MIO_EMAIL/MIO_PASSWORD) then auto-login (mints+stores a key, REPLACING any stored key); unauthenticated; in agents prefer a pre-provisioned MIO_API_KEY
mio whoami — print resolved user, active team, hub, api-base, profile, and key source; use as "did my setup work?" check
mio logout — clear stored credentials

mio config set — set a config value (keys: current_team, current_hub, api_base; validated as UUID / http(s) URL)
mio config get — get a config value
mio config list — list all config values

mio api-keys create — create a new API key for the current team (secret returned once)
mio api-keys list — list API keys for the current team
mio api-keys retrieve — retrieve a single API key by id
mio api-keys delete — revoke an API key by id

mio teams create — create a new team
mio teams list — list teams the authenticated user belongs to
mio teams retrieve — retrieve a team by id
mio teams update — update team attributes
mio teams delete — delete a team
mio teams switch — server-side team switch AND updates local CLI context (writes team to config, clears hub)
mio teams members list — list members of a team
mio teams members add — add a user to a team
mio teams members remove — remove a user from a team

mio users me — retrieve the authenticated user's own profile
mio users list — list users
mio users retrieve — retrieve a user by id
mio users update — update a user's attributes

mio roles create — create a custom role
mio roles list — list roles
mio roles retrieve — retrieve a role by id
mio roles update — update a role
mio roles delete — delete a role
mio roles permissions list — list all available permissions
mio roles permissions assign — assign a permission to a role by --slug (flat {slug} body; requires user-JWT auth, API keys are rejected 401)
mio roles permissions remove — remove a permission from a role (positional role_id + permission_slug; destructive, needs --yes; user-JWT only)

mio hubs * — the hub id is an OPTIONAL positional on every hubs verb except `delete`: precedence positional > --hub > current_hub in config > single-hub auto-default, so `mio hubs retrieve <id>`, `mio hubs retrieve --hub <id>` and a bare `mio hubs retrieve` are all valid. Covers retrieve/update/policies update/policies gate/redirect-origins get|set/email-settings get|update/navigation list|add|remove|reorder. When no hub resolves from any source the error names all three sources (never Cobra's "accepts 1 arg(s), received 0"). EXCEPTION: `hubs delete` still requires the id positionally — irreversible, so it never takes its target from ambient context (MIO-2732)
mio hubs create — create a new hub within the active team; author the presentation layer via --branding-json/--navigation-json/--settings-json/--meta-json (opaque JSONB objects; inline JSON or @file); --logo-url and --favicon-url merge into branding rather than replacing it. Unknown keys in --branding-json/--settings-json/--meta-json WARN by default (stderr) and ERROR under --strict-keys (best-effort allowlist — the API stores these blobs verbatim with no schema, and the hub frontend is the authoritative render contract; accepted keys are in each flag's --help and docs/internal/api-surface.md) (MIO-2515). EXCEPTION to "verbatim": ANY branding key ending in _url (case-insensitive, present or future) is validated server-side — on the CLI allowlist that is logo_url, favicon_url, social_image_url, auth_logo_url, custom_login_logo_url, custom_font_url (MIO-2658). Each must be null or a STRING (a list/dict raises), and a string must be an ABSOLUTE https:// URL; rejected are any other scheme (incl. plain http://, data:, javascript:), protocol-relative //host, relative paths, whitespace/control chars (raw OR percent-decoded), backslashes, user:pass@ credentials, percent-encoding in the host, and invalid ports — a 422, not a silent drop. Non-_url keys round-trip unchecked. Output includes a derived published (=!is_private); in table mode a private hub also prints a stderr hint with the slug and how to publish (--published). No public URL is echoed — the API returns no domain/url field and the CLI knows only the API base, so a URL is not derivable client-side (MIO-2521, MIO-2522)
mio hubs list — list hubs in the active team
mio hubs retrieve — retrieve a hub by id; output includes derived convenience booleans registration_enabled (=settings.registration.enabled===true, fail-closed) and published (=!is_private), mirroring the backend's derived policies_enabled; --raw bypasses them (MIO-2516, MIO-2521)
mio hubs update — update hub attributes; --navigation-json authors the header/footer menu (whole-blob replace, typed items validated); --branding-json/--settings-json/--meta-json deep-merge (read-modify-write, sibling keys preserved); --logo-url and --favicon-url merge into branding (all inline JSON or @file). --registration-enabled true|false sets settings.registration.enabled via RMW (gated on Changed() so =false ≠ unset; sibling keys preserved) (MIO-2516). --unset <dotted.path> DELETES a blob key (the only real delete — *-json flags are merge-only: null persists as null, {} is a no-op); first segment selects the blob (branding/settings/meta), nested paths supported, repeatable + comma-separated; blank/bare-blob/unknown-blob paths are usage errors that fire no request (MIO-2517). Apply order per blob: (1) *-json merge, (2) scalar flags, (3) --unset LAST (unset wins over a same-command merge). Unknown keys in the merged blobs WARN by default and ERROR under --strict-keys (only the keys you supply are checked, never the hub's existing stored blob; MIO-2515) ASYMMETRY (MIO-2811): settings.policies is accepted on hubs CREATE (policies.enabled/show) and SILENTLY DISCARDED on hubs UPDATE — the backend pops the key (app/hubs/service.py `incoming.pop("policies", None)`), so `hubs update --settings-json '{"policies":…}'` used to report success and change nothing. The CLI now WARNS on stderr (errors under --strict-keys, before any request). Real doors: `hubs policies gate` for enabled, `hubs policies update` for the documents, `hubs policies get` to read back. There is NO CLI door for policies.show on an existing hub.
mio hubs delete — delete a hub; the hub id MUST be positional (no --hub/current_hub fallback — irreversible)
mio hubs navigation list/add/remove/reorder — edit the hub menu item-by-item without rebuilding the whole --navigation-json blob (RMW the navigation blob: GET hub, mutate one bucket (siblings pass through byte-for-byte; only the edited bucket's item positions are renumbered, MIO-2990), PATCH navigation as a whole-blob replace). Buckets: header/footer/mobile. Items have no stable id → addressed by zero-based INDEX (from 'list'). add [hub_id] <bucket> takes --item-json '<obj>' (any bucket/type; NOT fully verbatim — a `position` key is normalized to the item's array index, MIO-2990; inline or @file) OR the url convenience --type url --href <h> --label <l> (header/footer only — mobile items {id,label,route,icon} must use --item-json), plus --position to insert (default append); remove [hub_id] <bucket> --index N; reorder [hub_id] <bucket> --order 2,0,1 (a permutation, every index once). The hub id shares the positional slot with the bucket: a lone header|footer|mobile is read as the BUCKET and the hub comes from --hub/current_hub (`mio hubs navigation add header --type url …`), so `list` accepts 0-2 positionals and add/remove/reorder 1-2 (MIO-2732). Item `icon` values are NOT validated by the CLI and use two different vocabularies — see the NAV ICON GLYPHS header note above (header/footer = the FE sprite ids, optional; mobile = an 8-name whitelist, mandatory). Re-validates the whole menu (typed header/footer items, hub-scoped hrefs) before writing; usage errors fire no PATCH. No optimistic-lock guard — last-write-wins, same as --navigation-json (MIO-2633)
mio hubs scaffold — build a full-experience hub in ONE idempotent command from a template: --template community applies branding+favicon, a typed navigation menu (hub-relative hrefs auto-scoped to /{slug}), settings.registration.enabled, discussion spaces, an onboarding contact-attribute schema, playlists (hub-scoped, published visible), and a homepage (page-builder catalog template → page create + tree set). Create mode: --name/--slug (a new private hub). Resume/target mode: --hub <id> (also resumes a partially-built hub — steps are idempotent: spaces/onboarding skip-if-exists, playlists skip if the hub already has published ones). --dry-run prints the ordered plan with no changes. --publish (default OFF; the hub stays private for review) sets is_private:false at the end. --favicon-url/--logo-url/--registration-enabled override the template. PALETTE (MIO-2604) — VERSION GATE: these flags and the machine-readable json result (MIO-2574) are NOT in v0.12.1, where they exit 2 with `unknown flag`: --primary-color/--secondary-color/--text-color/--background-color/--header-color/--header-accent/--social-image-url, plus --branding-json for a whole object, MERGE over the template's branding block (a key you do not name keeps the template's value); precedence is template → --branding-json → scalar flags, matching how --logo-url/--favicon-url already beat --branding-json on hubs update. CASCADE: --primary-color also fills header_color unless YOU gave a header color (--header-color, or a header_color key in --branding-json) — the template's own header_color does not suppress it, because the community template sets header_color to its primary and yielding to it would leave a rebranded hub with the template's header. Color VALUES are passed through unvalidated (branding is opaque JSONB with no server-side format contract to mirror, and the sibling --logo-url/--favicon-url ship no scheme check either), while the KEYS are strict-checked pre-auth against the MIO-2515 allowlist so a typo exits 2 with no request. NOTE the value contract is the FRONTEND's, not the API's: parseBranding accepts ONLY 6-digit #RRGGBB for the six color keys and silently falls back otherwise, so pass 6-digit hex even though nothing rejects anything else. --dry-run names the palette it would apply; the json result carries branding_overrides (the resolved layer, cascade included; {} when none). POLICIES + ENFORCEMENT GATE (MIO-2567) — VERSION GATE: NOT in v0.13.0 or earlier, where a scaffolded hub's ToS is written but never enforced (a freshly registered member reads tos_acceptance_required:false and POST .../tos/accept answers the enumeration-safe 404 that masks "gate not enabled"); repair those hubs with `mio hubs policies gate <hub_id> --enabled`. The policies step now writes each policy document (PATCH .../policies) AND THEN flips the hub-level enforcement gate (PATCH .../policies/gate, settings.policies.enabled) when the template declares `enabled: true`. Enforcement is ONE flag per hub, not one per policy — the backend stores no per-policy enabled — so the template's per-policy `enabled` values are COLLAPSED onto that single gate: they must agree, and a true alongside a false is rejected in the WRITE-FREE PREFLIGHT (exit 2 naming both keys, before the hub is created — the whole policies block is validated beside HubTemplate.Validate, not at pipeline stage 5). The gate write is ENABLE-ONLY, matching the ratified applier contract in mio-page-catalog catalog.schema.json ("MUST call PATCH .../policies/gate when enabled is true", silent on false): a template that declares none, or that resolves to false, writes NO gate and leaves the hub's current setting standing — narrated on stderr, never silent, because acting on a false would mean every resume disables enforcement an operator turned on by hand. Use `mio hubs policies gate <hub_id> --enabled=false` to actually disable one. Gate LAST, after the content writes, so members are never briefly asked to accept the default document the template is about to replace. NOTE settings.policies.* in a template is inert: the generic hub PATCH pops `policies` out of an incoming settings blob server-side, so the template's policies[] block is the only surface that reaches the gate (the ratified schema says so outright: "a settings-blob PATCH does not enforce"). RESUME CAVEAT — re-runs are NOT safe for policy CONTENT: applyHubPolicies always sends `content`, so a template that omits it (the shipped community one does) RESETS that policy to the backend default on every apply, and for a tos with require_acceptance that also normalizes the version, RE-PROMPTING every member who had already accepted. That reset predates MIO-2567; flipping the gate is what makes it member-visible. Re-apply hand-edited legal text after any resume with `mio hubs policies update <hub_id> --policy-type tos --content @tos.md --require-acceptance`. WELCOME POST (MIO-2558, VERSION GATE: lands in the release AFTER v0.13.0, unreleased as of this index; on v0.13.0 and earlier step 9 is a skip-with-note named `backend-gated`): the terminal step is now `welcome-post` and it POSTs the template's welcome discussion into one of the hub's own spaces. It is DECLARATIVE — it fires only when the hub template carries a `welcomePost` block ({space: <slug of one of its spaces>, title, body?, is_published?}); no shipped catalog declares one yet (community at 0.14.1 does not), so today the step is a plan-visible no-op and the CLI invents no post copy. Idempotent by TITLE within the target space (the endpoint has no upsert and no meta field to mark), so a resume adopts the existing post instead of creating a second one — and a welcome post you DELETED stays deleted. The title is compared and POSTED STRIPPED because the API stores title.strip(); the scan is hub-wide with the space matched client-side, because passing filter[space_id] would hide moderation-removed rows and duplicate the post. The json result carries welcome_post_id plus welcome_post_status (created|adopted|adopted_deleted; both null when the template declares none). CAVEAT: `adopted` does NOT mean the post is visible — the admin list never serializes is_removed, so a moderation-removed match reports as plain `adopted`; only soft-deletion (adopted_deleted) is detectable. Retrieve the id if visibility matters. The `welcomePost` key is NOT yet ratified catalog vocabulary (MIO-2812) — absent from mio-page-catalog's schema, it parses only via additionalProperties:true, so treat its shape as PROVISIONAL. Both failure modes are silent: a ratified spec landing under a different name/shape, or a typo like `welcomepost`, produces no validation error and no post — the step just reports "no welcome post in template" in the plan. The other formerly-deferred item, auto-assign-admin (MIO-2540), is server-side only — the backend does it on hub create, so the CLI has nothing to wire and no longer mentions it. Delegates to the existing CLI verbs' internals (CLI-only, no raw REST), so template values pass the same validation as the individual commands — a malformed key errors instead of silently dropping. Output honors -o json|table|plain like every other command (MIO-2574): json/plain (json is the default off a TTY) emit a machine-readable result — hub_id, hub_slug, hub_name, hub_path, published, template_id, catalog_revision, homepage_page_id, welcome_post_id, welcome_post_status, policy_gate (the enforcement gate this run WROTE — true, or null when it wrote none: no declaration, or a resolved false, both of which leave the hub's setting standing, since the write is enable-only; policies[] says the document exists, policy_gate says whether this run turned enforcement on), and pages/spaces/onboarding_attributes/playlists/policies carrying the ids this run created or recovered — so `mio hubs scaffold … -o plain --jq .hub_id` captures the new hub id directly (-o plain: --jq alone JSON-quotes a string, MIO-2792); table renders the human summary. Every progress note, catalog provenance line and recovery hint goes to stderr, so a json stdout is always parseable; if a step fails after the hub was created, the error itself names the hub id (nothing is rolled back). The public URL is host-relative — the API returns no domain/url (MIO-2543) SERVER-SIDE OP (MIO-2976): in create mode the run first PROBES POST /api/teams/{team_id}/hubs/from-template (type hub_scaffolds) and, when that op answers, the backend builds the whole hub in ONE transaction. The op ships DORMANT (HUB_SCAFFOLD_ENABLED default False), so today every run falls back to the client-side pipeline and behaviour is unchanged. It falls back only on the dormant signal (a bare 405 with Allow: GET); every other status surfaces, including the 404 template_not_found that shares exit 4 with it. ALWAYS client-side: --hub, --dry-run, a missing --name or --slug, --catalog, and any branding override (--branding-json or a palette flag such as --primary-color) — the op's overrides carry only logo_url/favicon_url/registration_enabled/publish. An empty (or whitespace-only) value for ANY branding key ending _url — however spelled: --logo-url/--favicon-url/--social-image-url, or --branding-json '{"logo_url":""}' — is a USAGE ERROR before any request (exit 2): the API rejects an empty branding *_url on hub create AND update, so neither path can honour it — routing it client-side would create the hub and then 422 at the blobs PATCH. Clear a branding key with `mio hubs update <hub_id> --unset branding.logo_url` instead. Every FLAG-forced skip is noted on stderr; --dry-run is not, being structural. The Idempotency-Key is deterministic (team+template+name+slug), so re-running the same command converges instead of creating a second hub; re-running the same name+slug after the backend's catalog pin moved, or with different override flags, is a 409 that applied nothing; the error text carries the literal token idempotency_fingerprint_mismatch in square brackets, which is what to branch on. -o json reports the same keys on both paths. STARTER-TEMPLATE VOCABULARY (MIO-3065): playlists are created SCOPED to the hub (hub_id — without it every playlist detail page 404s) at the template's own visibility, validated against the enum the CREATE takes (public|unlisted|private — the hub-media enum's `members` is NOT legal here); their per-hub publication row is a ratified hardcoded visibility:public (members-only day one is not template-expressible). playlists[].documents[] entries become synthetic READY document files (files/synthetic, MIO-2285) at the playlist's visibility, each with its OWN per-hub publication row (without which it is attached but discloses zero item cards to an anonymous viewer) and attached as items after the file_ids ones; file_ids[] media is attached, never published. spaces[].icon (sprite name, MIO-2802) reaches the space create. PLAYLIST dataSource FILL CONTRACT: a page node shipping dataSource {type:playlist,id:"",key:<playlists[].key>} gets that key resolved against the playlists this run created and the id written into id BEFORE the tree PUT (the hub renderer filters on a truthy ds.id and the backend compiler reads a present-but-empty id as ("container",""), so an unfilled node renders an empty band); a key naming no playlist of the same template is an exit-2 preflight failure before the hub exists, and a key still unfillable at apply time (a resume whose playlists step skipped and whose id could not be recovered by unambiguous title) fails the whole pages step with exit 2 BEFORE any page is written, rather than publishing a blank band and marking it applied. The server-side ops apply NONE of this (mio-backend parity: MIO-3073), so a template declaring spaces[].icon, playlists[].documents or a playlist dataSource key is applied client-side, announced on stderr.
mio hubs templates — list the hub templates the TARGET BACKEND's catalog offers (the CLI embeds none); honors -o json|table and --jq. --catalog <file> lists a local artifact instead — digest-verified and fail-closed, the same escape hatch hubs scaffold takes, so a catalog branch's templates can be listed and not only scaffolded (MIO-3065; before it this exited 2 with `unknown flag`)
mio hubs policies get — READ both policy documents + the enforcement gate AS STORED (MIO-2815); optional positional hub id (falls back to --hub/current_hub). GET /api/v1/teams/{team_id}/hubs/{hub}/policies — the team-owner ADMIN read (admin_get_hub_policies, MIO-2394), NOT the member-portal one, which serves defaults and forces enabled=true and so cannot answer 'is enforcement really on?'. Returns a LIST of {policy_type, content, version, enabled, require_acceptance}. ALWAYS exactly TWO items (tos, privacy_policy) — an unconfigured document is served with rendered DEFAULT TEXT, so there is NO empty case to handle. `enabled` is the ONE hub-level gate repeated per item, not per-policy. TRAP: `version` does NOT distinguish custom from default. The backend assigns a version ONLY for policy_type=tos AND ONLY when require_acceptance is set (app/hubs/service.py `if policy_type == "tos" and require_acceptance:`), and the read projects an absent version as "default-v1" — so a hand-written PRIVACY POLICY, or a tos saved without --require-acceptance, reads "default-v1" while holding custom text. Acting on that reading before a `hubs scaffold --hub` resume DESTROYS the text. `content` always has a value (stored, else the rendered default) so its presence proves nothing; `require_acceptance` is tri-state (true/false = a real edit was recorded; null = UNKNOWN, covering never-written AND pre-MIO-2523 documents). The only reliable check is to READ THE CONTENT AND LOOK AT IT. The resume reverts any policy its template declares no text for; the member re-prompt only follows for a tos saved WITH require_acceptance — anything else is replaced silently (MIO-2818). Capture the gate with `-o plain --jq '.[0].enabled'`; a bare `--jq .enabled` EXITS 1 with "expected an object but got: array", it does NOT yield null
mio hubs policies update — create or replace a hub legal policy (tos or privacy_policy); hub id is an OPTIONAL positional (falls back to --hub/current_hub); --content supports @file; --require-acceptance for tos only
mio hubs policies gate — toggle hub policy enforcement (settings.policies.enabled); optional positional hub id (falls back to --hub/current_hub); --enabled required and explicit (--enabled or --enabled=false). This is a SEPARATE write from `policies update`: content without the gate is a hub whose ToS exists and is never presented — the backend reads settings.policies.enabled by identity (only the JSON boolean true counts) and this endpoint is its only writer, so `hubs update --settings-json '{"policies":{"enabled":true}}'` is a silent no-op (the generic hub PATCH pops `policies`). An admin policies READ DOES exist — GET /api/v1/teams/{team_id}/hubs/{identifier}/policies (admin_get_hub_policies, MIO-2394), same owner credentials as this gate verb, reporting both documents with the ACTUAL stored gate state (the member-portal GET forces enabled=true for public display). This file previously said there was none. Read it with `mio hubs policies get` (MIO-2815) — which is how you check whether a `hubs scaffold` resume reverted hand-edited legal text. CAVEAT: `version` does NOT prove custom-vs-default (the backend versions ONLY tos AND ONLY with require_acceptance; everything else projects as "default-v1"), and `content` always has a value (yours, else the rendered default). Compare the CONTENT itself
mio hubs redirect-origins get — read the magic-link redirect-origin allowlist for a hub (owner-only; optional positional hub id, falls back to --hub/current_hub)
mio hubs redirect-origins set — full-replace the redirect-origin allowlist; optional positional hub id (falls back to --hub/current_hub); provide --origins (comma-separated) or --clear to empty it
mio hubs branding attach — attach an uploaded media file as a managed hub branding asset; hub id optional positional (falls back to --hub/current_hub); --file-id (FILE id, media_id resolved automatically) and --role logo|favicon|social_image|auth_logo required, optional --position. POST /api/v1/teams/{team_id}/hub-branding-attachments; replaces any prior asset for the same (hub, role); the resolved durable public CDN URL overlays branding.<role>_url at read time and is surfaced as resolved_public_url on the rendered attachment (stderr warning when not yet resolved). Client-side eligibility preflight mirrors the backend publish predicate (upload READY + raster image MIME; SVG exits 2 before the attach POST (the file GET that discovers the MIME has already fired) — the backend accepts the attach but never publishes an SVG, a silent no-op). Capture with -o plain --jq .resolved_public_url

mio content create — create a content node in a hub; media binding takes EITHER --media-id (the Media PK, .media_id from 'mio media files retrieve') OR --file-id (the FILE id, resolved to the Media PK for you) — mutually exclusive. PREFER --file-id: the backend stores media_id WITHOUT validating it (MIO-3432), so a file id passed to --media-id yields a lesson silently pointing at nothing (MIO-3074)
mio content list — list root-level content nodes in a hub
mio content retrieve — retrieve a content node by id
mio content children — list child nodes of a content node
mio content update — update a content node; same --media-id / --file-id media binding as create (mutually exclusive; prefer --file-id). An EMPTY value for either is REJECTED, not treated as 'unlink' — 'mio content update $ID --media-id "$MEDIA"' with $MEDIA unset would otherwise destroy a working link and exit 0 (cobra reports the flag as Changed, so a Changed-based guard does not catch it). To unlink deliberately pass --unset-media, a boolean no shell variable can expand into (MIO-3074)
mio content delete — soft-delete a content node
mio content restore — restore a soft-deleted content node
mio content reorder — reorder content nodes within a parent
mio content reconcile — create content nodes for a hub's media playlists (one container per playlist, one lesson per item) so their files gain progress/completion tracking, My List saves, comments, and the page builder's single-file feature binding; flags: --playlist-id (repeatable). Omit --playlist-id to use the playlists the hub was SCAFFOLDED with. A file living ONLY in a playlist has no content node and gets none of the above until this is run — and it is NEVER run for you. Additive: existing nodes are adopted, not duplicated. TWO LIMITS: a playlist must satisfy playlist.hub_id == this hub (a team-library playlist merely PUBLISHED into the hub 422s playlist_not_in_hub), and lessons land UNPUBLISHED unless the file AND its playlist are each already published to the hub (MIO-3074; backend MIO-3258)

mio pages create — create a page in a hub; flags: --title --slug --type --privacy (public|members|private) --position --is-home (sends is_homepage) --settings/--meta (@file). NO --published/--description/--layout (not in schema). --privacy DEFAULTS TO members: omit it and the page is login-walled, which is how a hub ships looking public and isn't (hubs scaffold sets it, MIO-2563; this manual path does not). `home` is a RESERVED slug (rejected) and an omitted --slug fails "Field required" — use a real slug (welcome/start/about) and designate the homepage with --is-home
mio pages list — list pages in a hub
mio pages retrieve — retrieve a page by id; add --tree to get the raw published node tree (page-trees resource, resolve=false) for admin editor use
mio pages update — update a page
mio pages delete — delete a page
mio pages home — retrieve the hub's home page
mio pages publish — publish a page draft; requires --if-match <draft_version> (read draft_version from a prior retrieve for optimistic concurrency)
mio pages sections create — add a section to a page; --type is validated against the catalog writable section types (see 'pages catalog section-types --writable-only')
mio pages sections list — list sections on a page
mio pages sections update — update a section
mio pages sections delete — delete a section from a page
mio pages sections reorder — reorder sections on a page
mio pages tree get — get a page's author draft node-tree (audience=author, resolve=true); draft_version is the OCC token for 'tree set'/'publish'. RESPONSE SHAPE ≠ WRITE SHAPE, and the fix is a RE-WRAP not an unwrap: get answers {"id":...,"tree":<the root NODE, BARE>,"draft_version":N} (the backend unwraps before answering — bare_node = resolved.get("root", resolved); its DTO says "the resolved draft tree ROOT node — bare (not wrapped in {root: ...})") while set --file REJECTS anything without a top-level root ("Tree must have a 'root' key at the top level."). So --jq .tree alone yields a file tree set refuses — use --jq '{root: .tree}'
mio pages tree set — replace a page's draft node-tree from --file (a tree JSON, {"root":{...}}); --if-match <draft_version> is OPTIONAL and defaults to 0 — omit it for the FIRST tree on a draft-less page (whose 'tree get' 404s, so there is no version to read back); pass the current draft_version for later sets (a defaulted 0 against a page that already has a draft is a 409 conflict, never a clobber). A page created by `hubs scaffold` ALREADY HAS A DRAFT (draft_version 1, not 0), so your first write against one needs --if-match 1 — never guess, read it back with `mio pages tree get <id> --jq .draft_version`. Every node needs an "id": scaffold mints fresh UUIDv7s, so splice scaffolded subtrees rather than hand-writing nodes (there is no id-minting helper); "root"/"hero" style outline markers are not valid ids
mio pages catalog * — the group has exactly THREE verbs: scaffold, templates, section-types. THERE IS NO `pages catalog list`
mio pages catalog scaffold — scaffold a node-tree from a catalog template (Go applier); --template <id> [--variant <v>]; page templates emit {"root":...} for 'tree set', section templates emit a bare node; emit-only (offline-capable; --offline forces vendored, --catalog <file> overrides). PAGE templates are OUTLINES: page-homepage's hero child arrives as {"kind":"row","template":"hero","settings":{}} with no surface and no values — scaffold the page for the skeleton, then scaffold each SECTION separately for the real DS-conformed recipe and splice it into root.children. `row` is the unified 1-4 column section; --variant picks the layout: 1col|2eq|2left|2right|3eq|4eq|bound-cards|cta-band|faq (hero/grid/compact carry variants too — `pages catalog templates` prints them)
mio pages catalog templates — list catalog author templates + their variants; --page-type <pt> shows the section templates recommended for that page type (ordered) + its page template
mio pages catalog section-types — list catalog compiled section types; --writable-only lists just the imperative-door allow-list

mio media files list — list team media files (cursor-paginated); --limit --after
mio media files retrieve — retrieve a media file by id (POSITIONAL)
mio media files durable-url — print a file's durable (non-expiring) hub-scoped image URL(s) to inline into a page-tree image node; joins durable_variants[preset] with the REQUIRED ?hub_id=; --hub required, --preset (omit=all presets), --publish also publishes the file public to the hub so the URL resolves; image-only (MIO-2514, backend MIO-2525/#533)
mio media files update — update file metadata; --title --description --visibility --folder-id
mio media files delete — soft-delete a file; --yes
mio media files upload — upload a file end-to-end from the CLI (create → presigned S3 PUT → finalize; auto-multipart for large files); path is POSITIONAL; --title --mime-type --folder-id --wait --timeout --multipart --part-size-mb. **`--wait` and video transcoding (MIO-3001):** `--wait` blocks until upload AND transcode are done, but a null `status_transcode` means two different things and only one of them is "nothing to wait for". A freshly finalized VIDEO reads null for a window — the backend's finalize sets `status_upload: READY` and EMITS `MediaUploaded`; a best-effort handler enqueues the transcode job, and only that job sets `status_transcode` — so returning on the first null poll hands back an untranscoded file. `--wait` therefore keeps polling while `mime_type` is `video/*` (an exact proxy for the backend's own `asset_kind`, which is not serialized). It does NOT wait indefinitely: the transcode dispatch is gated on `FEATURE_MEDIA_VIDEO_ENABLED`, which defaults False and is false in PRODUCTION until P10, so on those backends the status stays null FOREVER and waiting for it would burn the whole `--timeout` and then FAIL. **The exact contract, which is a bound and NOT a guarantee:** the wait for a transcode to *appear* is capped at 30s (measured from `status_upload` reaching READY, and further capped by `--timeout`, whichever is smaller); once a transcode does appear, `--wait` follows it to READY under `--timeout`. Both caps are checked at POLL BOUNDARIES, so the real wall-clock bound is the cap plus up to one 2s poll interval — budget `--timeout 1s` and expect ~2s, not 1s. If nothing appears within that window the command returns **exit 0** — the upload genuinely succeeded — and warns on stderr, naming the window it actually waited. Do NOT read that warning as proof video is disabled: a backed-up transcode queue produces it too (`MEDIA_WORKER_MAX_JOBS` is 10), and the file may transcode moments later. Re-check with `mio media files retrieve <id>` rather than treating exit 0 as "transcoded". Non-video is unaffected — image/pdf/**audio** all have a permanently-null transcode status and return as soon as the upload is READY. A file reporting NO `mime_type` cannot be classified: it returns without waiting and says so. A FAILED transcode is still an error. `--wait` also blocks on `status_transcribe`, and that field has TERMINAL values that are neither null nor READY: `NOT_APPLICABLE` (literally `"READY" if words else "NOT_APPLICABLE"`, in both the auto path `app/media/transcription_service.py` and the admin re-transcribe path — the NORMAL outcome for a video with no speech) and `REJECTED`. Those are treated as settled; waiting for them to become READY would burn the whole `--timeout` and exit 1 on an upload that fully succeeded. `PENDING` — the only in-flight value this field actually takes — is still waited on, and `FAILED` is still an error. (MIO-2571's "null means not applicable" reading is unchanged — this is about non-null terminal values.)
mio media files replace — replace an existing file's underlying asset; <file_id> <path> POSITIONAL; single-part finalizes at .../replace/{replacement_id}/finalize, but multipart replace ENDS at the terminal .../replace/{replacement_id}/multipart/{upload_id}/complete (no separate finalize); --mime-type --filename --multipart --part-size-mb

mio media transcripts versions — list transcript versions, or retrieve one; media_id POSITIONAL, optional [version]
mio media transcripts edit — replace a transcript's words (creates a new version); media_id POSITIONAL; --words (JSON array or @file) --language
mio media transcripts revert — revert a transcript to a prior version; media_id POSITIONAL; --version (required, >= 1)

mio community discussions list — list a hub's discussions (admin view: includes drafts and soft-deleted); --filter-space (→ filter[space_id]) --limit --after. TRAP (MIO-2816): --filter-status sends filter[status], which admin_list_discussions does not accept — FastAPI ignores unknown query params, so it is a SILENT NO-OP that returns the unfiltered list, not an error. Filter client-side on .attributes.status (published|scheduled|draft) instead. The endpoint's other real filter, filter[is_broadcast], has no flag. NOTE the filtered branch (--filter-space) runs list_for_space, which hides moderation-REMOVED rows; the unfiltered list is the only view that shows them
mio community discussions create — VERSION GATE (MIO-2808): lands in the release AFTER v0.13.0 (unreleased as of this index); on v0.13.0 and earlier it exits 2 with `unknown command`. Post a discussion into a hub space (the admin welcome-post route). REQUIRED --space-id --title; optional --body, --is-published=false for a draft (omitted = published, the API default). The AUTHOR is derived server-side from your credentials (a team-owner key posts as the team owner's contact) — there is deliberately NO author flag, and the API rejects a smuggled author field with 422; authoring as an arbitrary member has no HTTP surface at all. The post lands in the target space regardless of that space's posting_permission (admin write). Title max 280 chars, non-blank — enforced server-side (422), not client-side
mio community discussions retrieve — retrieve a discussion by id (admin view). **DERIVED `deleted` (MIO-3022):** the admin views return soft-deleted rows on purpose (the repository takes `include_deleted` and the admin router passes it True — that is what makes this the one view carrying drafts, tombstoned AND moderation-removed rows, which the scaffold's welcome-post idempotency scan depends on). But the API's computed `status` is only published/scheduled/draft — it has NO "deleted" value — so a tombstoned discussion comes back as `status: "published"` with a non-null `deleted_at` beside it. The CLI therefore derives a boolean `deleted` on list/retrieve/create/update. `status` is NOT overwritten (it records what the row was before deletion) and `--raw` bypasses the derivation. Only injected when `deleted_at` is PRESENT: an absent key means the server did not say, and a synthesized `false` would be indistinguishable from a real one. This is why `delete` looked broken — it works, it is a SOFT delete, and a second delete of the same row is a legitimate 404.
mio community discussions update — set MODERATION state only: --is-pinned/--is-locked/--is-broadcast. Title/body are author-owned and NOT admin-editable — there are no --title/--body flags on update (there are on create)
mio community discussions delete — soft-delete a discussion (destructive, needs --yes). SOFT delete: the row keeps coming back from list/retrieve with `deleted: true` — it is not gone, it is tombstoned. Deleting an already-deleted discussion is a 404 (exit 4), which is correct, not a bug.

mio products create — create a product
mio products list — list products in the active team
mio products retrieve — retrieve a product by id
mio products update — update a product
mio products delete — delete a product
mio products prices create — create a price for a product; product id is a POSITIONAL arg. REQUIRED: --amount (minor units) --currency (usd|cad|gbp|eur|aud) --type (one_time|recurring); --interval (month|year|week|day) and --interval-count (>=1) are REQUIRED when --type=recurring. Optional: --name (label, <=100) --description (<=500) --is-active (default true). There is NO --nickname. e.g. mio products prices create <product_id> --amount 4900 --currency usd --type recurring --interval month --interval-count 1
mio products prices list — list prices for a product; product id is a POSITIONAL arg: mio products prices list <product_id>
mio products prices retrieve — retrieve a price by id
mio products prices update — update a price
mio products prices delete — delete a price

mio checkout subscriptions retrieve — retrieve a subscription by id
mio checkout subscriptions cancel — cancel a subscription
mio checkout payments list — list payments in a hub
mio checkout payments retrieve — retrieve a payment by id
mio checkout payments refund — issue a refund for a payment
mio checkout webhooks list — list payment webhook events
mio checkout webhooks retrieve — retrieve a webhook event by id
mio checkout webhooks replay — replay a payment webhook event
mio checkout accounts list — list connected payment accounts
mio checkout accounts retrieve — retrieve a payment account by id
mio checkout accounts onboarding-link — WEB/JWT-ONLY, always fails from this CLI (exit 3): the backend rejects API-key principals on this route (leaked key must not attach a payout account) and this CLI is API-key-only; connect Stripe via the member.dev dashboard instead
mio checkout stripe-sync import — start a Stripe data import for the active team
mio checkout stripe-sync import-status — check the status of a Stripe import run
mio checkout stripe-sync adopt-product — adopt an existing Stripe product into mio

mio email steps delete — delete a step from a drip campaign

mio email enrollments list — list contacts enrolled in a drip campaign

mio email stats get — retrieve email send/open/click stats for a hub
mio email suppressions list — list active email suppressions for the active hub
mio email suppressions create — suppress (admin_block) an email address for the active hub via --email; reason is forced to admin_block server-side
mio email suppressions lift — lift (un-suppress) a hub suppression by id; destructive, needs --yes. NOTE: the hub suppression routes require platform_admin, so team-admin API keys get 403
